To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of the multivariate likelihood refinement target in automated model building is more accurate than the currently used refinement target, (2) the multivariate likelihood approach is applicable to a wider range of SAD data sets and (3) the multivariate approach can be used to build high-resolution structures from low-signal SAD data.
the SAD refinement target extends the resolution and quality limits needed for successful model building with iterative methods.

(i) the multivariate likelihood refinement target is more theoretically valid than the current refinement functions, (ii) the multivariate refinement target extends the resolution and the phase-quality limits needed to obtain successful automated model building and (iii) the multivariate target is consistently better than the currently used refinement targets in terms both of the quality of models obtained and the percentage of residues built.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a new approach for automated model building with SAD data, and the results clearly show that the new method is superior to the current methods.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SAD multivariable likelihood function is the best choice for refinement with prior phase information.
the multivariate likelihood target is a better target than the others tested in the present work, and that this is especially true when the data are weak and/or at high resolution.
the SAD multivariable likelihood function is the best refinement target for automated model building with the current SIR2013 program.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multivariate likelihood functions are a better choice than the current functions and should be used for all SAD refinement.
, in order to achieve a high-quality model in automated model building, the prior phase information from the experimental SAD data should be used in the refinement procedure.
the multivariate likelihood functions should be preferred over the current refinement targets for automated model building with SAD data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multivariate likelihood approach should be used as the standard for automated model building with refinement.
the SAD multivariable likelihood function is an important refinement target for automated model building with SAD data and should be used routinely.

the SAD multivariant likelihood function can provide a more theoretically valid and accurate way of incorporating prior information in refinement, and thus should be considered as the standard for future model-building and refinement protocols.
